utterance: Hi Chloe, I’m Dr Smith. I understand it’s burning when you wee. Can you tell me more about what’s been happening since yesterday?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It stings and burns, especially right at the end, and I am going constantly every half hour with only a little bit coming out and have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present
Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills, pain in your back or sides, vomiting, or felt generally unwell? Any pain low in your tummy?
reply: I have no fevers or shivers and feel fine apart from this, with no pain in my back, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. I am eating normally and have not been sick, and there is just that low ache above my bladder and nothing else.

Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)
Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell
Red flag excluded: Abdominal pain beyond a low ache

utterance: Any vaginal discharge, itching, sores, or bleeding between periods or after sex? Does sex cause any pain?
reply: I have not had any discharge, itching, or sores like that, and I never bleed between my periods or after sex, which has also never been painful for me.

awards.label: Bleeding after sex or between periods

utterance: When was your last period, and was it normal? Is there any chance of pregnancy, including any missed pills?
reply: My last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal. I don't think I am pregnant because I am on the pill and I do not miss it.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: I ask everyone with these symptoms about sexual health because some infections can feel similar. Have you had a new partner recently, and do you use condoms? When was your last sexual health check?
reply: I have a boyfriend and we have been together for about a year, and it is just him. We do not use condoms because I am on the pill.

utterance: When did you last have a urine infection, how often have they happened, and did treatment work? Have you ever had a kidney infection or been told an antibiotic wouldn’t work for your urine infection?
reply: I had one UTI about two years ago, that is it, and I have never had anything like kidney problems. I am not allergic to anything that I know of.

utterance: Do you remember which antibiotic you took and whether it cleared things up? Have you taken any antibiotics recently or anything for these symptoms?
reply: I do not remember the name of the antibiotic from two years ago, but I have not had any antibiotics this year, nor have I taken anything for these current symptoms.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months

utterance: Do you have any kidney problems, diabetes, or conditions affecting your immune system, and do you take any medicines or supplements apart from your pill? Have you ever had a sexual health check?
reply: I do not have diabetes or any issues with my immune system, and I only take the combined oral contraceptive pill. I have never had a sexual health check.

utterance: This sounds most like a bladder infection. With your permission I’ll check your temperature and pulse and gently feel your tummy and back. A vaginal examination isn’t needed from what you’ve told me. Could you also provide a midstream urine sample—start weeing into the toilet, then collect some in the pot?
reply: Can we just do a script? I really need to get back to the café.

utterance: I understand you’re in a hurry. These checks only take a few minutes and help make sure it’s safe to treat as a simple bladder infection. We can start treatment today without waiting for laboratory results. Is that okay?
reply: Alright, let us just get it done then so I can get back to work.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Your urine check supports a bladder infection, and your examination shows no signs of a kidney infection. A short antibiotic course is appropriate. Because you’re under 25 and haven’t been screened, I also recommend a confidential chlamydia and gonorrhoea test, even without symptoms; a self-collected vaginal swab is easy and doesn’t need an examination. Would you like that today? We can also check a urine pregnancy test to be safe—would that be okay?
reply: Oh, okay. Can we just do the quick swab thing for that then? I really need to get going soon.

utterance: Yes, the self-collected swab is fine. Are you also happy for us to do the quick pregnancy check on your urine sample?
reply: Yeah, that is fine. Can you write the script now so I can go?

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Your pregnancy test is negative. I’ve prescribed nitrofurantoin: one 100 mg capsule four times a day with food for five days. Finish the course. It can cause nausea and turn your urine dark yellow or brown, which is harmless. If you develop a rash, stop it and seek advice; breathing difficulty or swelling needs urgent help. It won’t reduce the pill’s effectiveness, but vomiting or severe diarrhoea can—follow your pill’s missed-dose advice if that happens.

Drink normally to avoid dehydration; you don’t need to force extra water. You can use paracetamol as directed on the packet for discomfort. You should start feeling better within 48 hours. If you’re not improving by then, or symptoms return after treatment, come back so we can send a urine sample to the laboratory and review treatment.

Seek urgent medical care today if you develop fever, shivering, back or side pain, vomiting, or worsening tummy pain, as these can mean a kidney infection. Go to emergency if you become very unwell or cannot keep fluids down.

We’ll contact you about the swab result in about two days; please call if you haven’t heard. A positive result would need different treatment and partner advice. Any questions about the treatment before you go?
reply: No questions, I just really need to get back to the café now.
